sections.title: Executive verdict
sections.text:
Acetech is an inventory- and advertising-funded e-commerce trader, now attempting cross-border digital-brand acquisitions, not an asset-light software compounder. FY 2026 consolidated revenue grew 17.76% to₹82.7625 crore and PAT reached₹10.2784 crore, but CFO was−₹26.3119 crore. Post-March announced acquisition agreements total USD 4.208776 million with no target turnover disclosed. March cash cannot establish October funding capacity. The assessment is Hold—unresolved acquisition economics/funding, with severe exit constraints, not a finding of fraud or actual default. Quality scores remain low; IAS is NS pending the current cash/commitment bridge. [A 26][LUM][ZEN][NEO]

Model correction dated20 October2026: opening obligations and terminal claims have been reconciled separately from new forecast expenses. Reported historical financial statements are unchanged. The corrected scenario values are in section10.

sections.title: Research header, gates and confidence
sections.text: Acetech E-Commerce Limited, NSE SME ACETEC, ISIN INE1J6M01010; former Acetech Ventures Limited/LLP. Cutoff 20 October 2026, five-year horizon,15% nominal equity hurdle before investor taxes and illustrative₹5 lakh liquidity reference. Accounts use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, consolidated with wholly owned Conceptive Brains Private Limited and Acetech Ventures Inc. The small foreign subsidiary relies on management-provided financial data: assets₹0.2556 crore and revenue₹0.4203 crore. Official 19 October SM close₹130 ×1.6383735 crore shares gives₹212.9886 crore equity value. Historical operating/quality evidence is Medium; acquisition valuation and current funding are Low. G 1 conditional, G 2 hold for material current asset/earnings reconciliation, G 3 hold for acquisition funding, G 4 conditional due extreme thinness rather than proven suspension. [A 26][SH][BHAV]

sections.title: Scorecard and calculation audit
sections.text: Canonical judgments: GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 7, DUR 4, CAP 3, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 3, EARN 5. Exact v 3.0 weights give BQS 3.76; raw Growth Quality 5.00, with persistent weak-cash cap 5 explicitly retained. IAS R is NS; D 2, P 3, L 1 and Q=3.76 contribute a known weighted sum 1.74 at 65% coverage, so raw missingness bounds are 2.09–5.24, not a substituted midpoint. Composite arithmetic and supporting evidence IDs are attached. Material acquisition/funding holds exclude all investable ranking eligibility. Historical factors use bounded adverse evidence, while uncorroborated acquired-business economics remain unscored. [A 26][IPO][CORR][LUM][ZEN][NEO][BHAV]

sections.title: Business overview
sections.text: Goods sold through marketplaces, direct channels and B 2 B customers are the core revenue; recognition is on transfer of risks/rewards, net of GST and returns. FY 2026 goods₹81.2902 crore versus₹66.7613, while service revenue fell from₹3.5169 to₹1.4723. Total growth is not recurring subscription revenue. Business-promotion expense₹16.8240 crore plus advertising₹0.6884, compared with₹11.1107 and₹0.2631, shows the importance of paid customer acquisition. No verified cohort retention, CAC or lifetime-value data supports a recurring-revenue moat. Manufacturing is outsourced; logistics, sourcing, platform access, stock and promotion drive economics. The new overseas acquisitions concern Shopify lighting/decor and men’s apparel storefronts, with no disclosed target revenue, gross margin or customer-return data. [A 26][IPO][LUM][ZEN][NEO]

sections.title: Moat, industry and peers
sections.text: Prospectus top 10 customers/platform accounts were 98.19%/94.29%/92.65% in FY 2023/24/25 and 85.20% in H 1 FY 2026; largest 44.43% in FY 2025 and 40.87% in H 1, second 26.43%/27.62%. Accounts aggregating marketplace/state transactions are not unique end-consumer cohorts, so the 782-customer count is not evidence of broad consumer diversification. Supplier 1 represented 47.57% in FY 2025 and 44.90% in H 1; supplier 2 was 23.74% in H 1. No long-term customer/supplier contracts establish durable pricing power. The prospectus’s closest listed comparator is Pace E-Commerce: its issuer-compiled FY 2025 revenue₹72.1387 crore, EBITDA margin 5.92% and PAT margin 4.59% differ substantially from Acetech’s restated 13.29%/9.79%. This is a historical prospectus comparison, not independently updated peer valuation. No three-to-five genuinely comparable, verified peer set was established; forcing software/marketplace multiples onto an inventory trader would mislead. MOAT 3 reflects access and execution capability without demonstrated structural protection. [IPO]

sections.title: Revenue growth and historical comparability
sections.text: Combined/restated revenue FY 2023/24/25 is₹52.3782/60.2482/70.2805 crore; FY 2026 statutory consolidated₹82.7625 gives three-year CAGR 16.47%, with additions₹7.8700/10.0323/12.4820. FY 2025 later annual comparative is₹70.2782, a small presentation difference. REV 7 follows the 15–20% band; no trajectory bonus. The company converted from LLP in February 2024, but the LLP continued transactions through September 2024 while GST registrations transitioned. New-company standalone FY 2024 or FY 2025 cannot be spliced into a full business growth series. FY 2026 standalone₹79.5876 versus₹52.7341 also must not substitute for group growth. Restated PAT FY 2023/24/25₹1.5156/4.0214/6.8797 differs from original/re-audited₹2.5155/4.3518/7.0504 through tax, gratuity, depreciation, issue costs and other adjustments. FY 2026 returns to the₹7.0504 comparative. Only four comparable revenue observations exist, not a five-year CAGR. [IPO][A 24][A 25][A 26]

sections.title: Growth quality and reinvestment runway
sections.text: Online distribution offers a large addressable market, but accessible growth needs inventory, supplier advances, promotion and actual collections. FY 2026 closing receivables₹28.3344, inventory₹14.4286 and supplier advances₹7.4583 absorb₹50.2213 crore before payables. Equity/debt less cash/short-term FD gives closing capital proxy₹47.2314 versus₹13.1863. Incremental core EBIT₹4.5041 ×75% tax-normalization /₹34.0451 added capital is 9.92%, below an explicitly assumed 12–16% capital-cost range. This one-year proxy includes IPO timing and working-capital investment; it is not a project IRR. At unchanged FY 2025 core EBIT margin 13.48%, added revenue would generate only about 3.71% incremental after-tax return on that capital. CAP 3 and CASH 2 prevent a high-growth-quality label. Cross-border acquisitions may change the result, but undisclosed unit economics cannot be credited as an attractive reinvestment runway. [A 26][IPO]

sections.title: Management, governance and execution
sections.text: PDMS’s financial/IFC opinions are unmodified and audit-trail reporting is affirmative; that is not blanket governance clearance. Original FY 2024 accounts described₹2.4330 crore partner/friend balances as deemed deposits; prospectus FY 2025 cash flow shows repayment, so the old observation is not assumed to remain outstanding. June results required resubmission for missing segment/working-capital certificate and readability; August board explicitly acknowledged an exchange SOP fine for delayed FY 2026 results, amount not established. Annual management text contains unremoved editorial instructions, a reporting-quality warning rather than an attribution about authorship. Independent director Manish Rawal’s letter was dated/effective 21 May and accepted 2 June; the 3 June board filing uses 2 June cessation. Personal commitments are the stated reason, not an evidenced dispute; Umesh Mane replaced him. March promoter group 64.39%, Sweta 63.95%, no declared encumbrance/convertibles/warrants/ESOPs. All promoter shares and 25.1% of public shares were locked in at March, not a perpetual free-float estimate. [A 26][A 24][IPO][CORR][AUG][DIR][RES][SH]

sections.title: Financial forensics and related parties
sections.text: FY 2026 PBT₹13.9045, finance₹0.0827, depreciation₹0.0273, other income₹0.0084 imply core EBIT₹13.9788 and EBITDA₹14.0061. Removing other income gives core PAT₹9.7273–10.4221 at 30–25% tax; it does not resolve receivable recoverability. Full closing-share EPS₹6.2735 is below weighted₹8.44; old pre-bonus EPS₹108.28 is not comparable. CFO−₹26.3119 versus FY 2025+₹0.1989 gives two-year ratio of sums−150.69% against PAT₹17.3288. Prospectus three-year CFO₹0.4457/−0.4757/−1.0619 is a distinct restated series; FY 2025 current-investment classification₹1.1957 partly explains the later difference, not a fully reconciled bridge. FY 2026 CFO includes₹3.004 short-term FD purchase; removing that classification still leaves−₹23.3079. Trade receivables consume₹17.5911, inventory₹7.8928, supplier advances₹6.2952 and payables reduction₹2.4553. Cash capex only₹0.0027 cannot explain weak CFO; reported FCF−₹26.3146. Receivables over six months rose₹0.2674→₹6.3662, with no allowance; average-balance DSO using total sales proxy 86.17 days. Related loans from Sweta₹3.4506, Vijay₹0.0122 and Truelines₹0.6438 were taken and repaid, year-end nil. RPT purchases from Good Times₹1.7877 and sales to Modern₹0.5127 are inclusive of GST; they are not automatically abusive. Remuneration accrued and remuneration paid are separate columns and must not be added twice. [A 26][IPO][A 25]

sections.title: Valuation, IPO proceeds and linked scenarios
sections.text:
At₹130, equity₹212.9886 crore is 20.72 x reported PAT, or 20.44–21.90 x the narrow normalized range, before acquired-business effects. March₹19.6187 cash and₹3.0040 short-term FD are not all surplus: IPO utilization certificate leaves₹19.3348, comprising₹6 marketing,₹1.8122 WC and₹11.5226 acquisition/GCP. Original gross issue₹48.9485, revised certificate issue expense₹5.8738; revised objects differ modestly from prospectus and net share-cash bridge needs reconciliation. April Lumi Art USD 333776, July Zentaro/Phoenix USD 2075000 and September Neora USD 1800000 total USD 4.208776 m. Analyst FX 80–100, not a retrieved spot rate, implies₹33.6702–42.0878 crore. Neither target turnover nor realized cash contribution is disclosed. Five annual legacy-business paths start from actual March cash/FD, zero debt and₹49.3611 core WC, charge acquisitions once and marketing separately, and assume no rescue financing. Base 15/12/10/8/8% growth,16% EBIT margin yields₹23.0568 crore maximum gap at FX 90; bull 25/20/15/12/10%,20% margin and 30% opening-AR collection still gaps₹15.8393; bear 30% revenue loss,8–12% margin and linked collection/inventory stress gaps₹37.0729. No IRR is assigned to an unfunded path. Base FX80/100 gaps ₹18.8480/27.2656; overlap of additional marketing with existing margin spending can lower gaps by up to₹6. These are stress illustrations, not actual arrears or proof of insolvency. Current collections, payment installments, target cash flows and funding facilities could change them materially. R remains NS rather than inventing a target return. [A 26][CORR][IPO][LUM][ZEN][NEO][BHAV]

Model correction, 20 October 2026: this changes our cash-flow/terminal-claim treatment, not the issuer’s reported history. Pay consolidated income-tax provision ₹3.6262 crore, statutory TDS/professional-tax dues ₹0.4143 crore and current gratuity ₹0.0119 crore once: ₹4.0524 crore. No consolidated income-tax credit is established; a standalone credit label cannot offset a consolidated liability. Other ordinary current balances ₹0.4344 crore are retained as a constant operating stock, with accelerated settlement separately tested. Retain noncurrent gratuity ₹0.1436 crore as a terminal claim if value is assigned; the acquisition model already withholds an investor IRR. Printed current-provision components and subtotal differ by ₹0.0001 crore rounding. Corrected linked scenarios: Base: no terminal valuation assigned; peak funding gap ₹23.0568 crore; no investable IRR. Bull: no terminal valuation assigned; peak funding gap ₹15.8393 crore; no investable IRR. Bear: no terminal valuation assigned; peak funding gap ₹37.0729 crore; no investable IRR. [A26]

sections.title: Bear case and permanent-loss path
sections.text: The thesis-break variable is cash collection relative to acquisition cash commitments. A platform/customer loss can reduce sales, force more promotion, slow debtor collections and strand inventory while overseas installments still fall due. March contingent liabilities₹6.9421 crore include₹5.8006 GST demand and₹1.1415 other tax matters. July unblocking₹5.083352 crore IGST credit is favorable, but is neither cash income nor proof that every demand is extinguished; the relation to the contingent-demand schedule is unverified. Prospectus also flags the LLP GST transition and associated penalty risk. The bear model’s₹2 crore compliance/supplier cash shock is an assumption, not addition of the full contingent liability or a second debt claim. D 2 reflects severe plausible financing/dilution/impairment exposure on verified opening inputs, with high forecast uncertainty. The strongest contrary evidence is the debt-free March balance sheet, real revenue growth and favorable GST-credit action; these do not prove current acquisitions are funded. [A 26][IPO][GST][LUM][ZEN][NEO]

sections.title: Fivefold/tenfold feasibility and market expectations
sections.text: At unchanged net margin, share count and P/E,5 x in five years requires 37.97% annual revenue growth and 10 x 58.49%, versus verified 16.47% three-year growth. A 20% terminal-multiple compression raises required earnings growth further; acquisitions must be funded and converted into per-share cash earnings, not merely announced. No disclosed target sales, acquisition return bridge, durable customer retention or demonstrated cash conversion supports a credible multibagger case. Classification: speculative/unsupported, not impossible. P 3 reflects a roughly 21 x earnings price for cash-negative growth and opaque acquisition economics, not a claim that low nominal share price means cheap. [A 26][IPO][BHAV][LUM][ZEN][NEO]

sections.title: Liquidity and monitoring plan
sections.text: Official 60-session window 24 July–19 October includes 26 absent sessions after the March listing, treated as zero trading; mean turnover₹982725, median₹167700. At 5% of the lower statistic,₹5 lakh needs 59.63 sessions;2%/10% participation gives 149.08/29.82. Last 20 sessions have 7 absent days, mean₹930576, median₹405720 and 24.65 days at 5%. L 1 is the rubric floor, not a suspension finding. One 1200-share lot costs₹156000 at₹130;3/4 lots are₹468000/₹624000. Official band 20%, current SM series; named surveillance absence is not blanket clearance and live spread/depth is unavailable. Monitor: (1) actual cash and collection bridge against March AR₹28.3344; worsening aged AR above₹6.3662 is an alert; (2) Lumi Art completion/consideration reconciliation, promised 30 days from April 8; (3) Neora final handover scheduled Oct 22; (4) Zentaro/Phoenix final installment Jan 7,2027; (5) target audited sales/returns and purchase-price allocation before crediting growth; (6) IPO objects and FD availability; (7) GST-credit utilization and demand reconciliation; (8) comparable H 1 FY 2026–27 CFO and inventory; (9) fresh leverage/dilution and RPT balances; (10) sustained turnover improvement, not a single block trade. Unfunded commitments or material unrecoverable receivables would be thesis breaks; mere price volatility is not. [BHAV][BAND][SEC][ESM][A 26][CORR][LUM][ZEN][NEO][GST] The October 19 REG1 file applies to October 21, not retroactively to the latest trade. Active cautions: Less than 100 unique PAN traded in previous 30 days; SME scrip is not regularly traded. The SME caution is reported as an exchange flag, not evidence of additional zero-trading days or wrongdoing. It does not mechanically change the turnover-based L score.

sections.title: Final classification and conditional action
sections.text: Hold—unresolved, low-quality speculative acquisition transition. BQS/GQS are historical quality judgments, not eligible investment rankings while critical current evidence is missing; IAS remains NS despite a verified price and scoreable poor liquidity. The company does not satisfy compounder criteria. Lower price alone cannot resolve unknown target cash flows, installment funding or aged-debtor realization. A favorable reassessment requires a reconciled current balance sheet, credible acquisition cash returns and funding, improved audited cash conversion, resolved material reporting differences and practical tradability. This is research prioritization, not an instruction to trade or an invented portfolio allocation.

sections.title: Sources, assumptions and open questions
sections.text: All monetary figures are INR crore unless explicitly stated. Annual and prospectus sources were read directly, with scanned notes visually checked; web-render failures were resolved through the same public issuer/exchange PDFs. Annual 2024 was partial and is used only for narrow legacy observations. Primary March shareholding confirms SME identity and capital; no personal tax IDs are reproduced. Restated and later statutory histories remain separate. Material open questions: exact net issue-proceeds bridge; FY 2025 CFO classification/reconciliation; current receivable recoveries and short-term FD availability; acquisition payments, signed closing status and target economics; GST-credit/demand overlap; current ownership and any new facilities. No undisclosed target profits, automatic funding rescue, converted legal permission into cash, or current price from the undated input CSV is used. Model assumptions and evidence audit are attached.

model_correction_2026_10_20.ordinary_stock_policy: The identified ordinary operating payable stock is held constant in nominal rupees in the reference opening and every forecast closing balance. The stated incremental WC forecast is after this constant stock; accelerated-settlement sensitivity reduces the stock to zero once and never charges it again.
